summary.intent: Fix a login page glitch where the email button shows 'sending code' while a Google login is in progress, and file issues for the problem.
summary.outcome: Made EmailLoginForm and the Google button each own their in-flight state instead of using the host-wide busy flag. Added tests, filed two issues (bug, comp:web), and committed per issue. A browser check of the fix via the dev server was started but not finished in the transcript.

repo: packages/auth-ui hosts login buttons (email form, Google button, wallet button); the hosts passed one shared `busy` flag that drove both blocking and labels, so each button showed the other's in-flight state.
The API verifies a Google ID token rather than exchanging an auth code, so a custom-styled Google trigger would need an API change.
Issue convention for bugs: labels `bug` + `comp:web`, no milestone.
The repo's convention is one commit per filed issue.
Older Google button tests passed mocks returning no promise, which broke once the button awaited the handler; a `false` hidden attribute value also needed adjusting in tests.
There is an unrelated pre-existing typecheck error in the repo.

code.finding: The form received a host-wide `busy` used for both blocking and the button label; it now tracks its own in-flight state for the 'sending code' label.

workflow: Consulted an advisor before changing code, then checked the sibling components for the same bug (the Google button had the mirror problem).
Ran independent checks (typecheck, lint, label/milestone listing, dev server probe) in parallel.
Read memory notes on issue-filing conventions before creating issues.

friction: Existing Google button tests needed mock fixes after the async change, which took several test-rerun iterations.
